output.reason: The brief makes a convincing case that the problem sits with Kestrel: 8 of the 11 associates on it resigned, against 1 of the 13 who weren't, and that rules out pay or the firm-wide hours target as the main cause. It's also honest that it can't yet tell workload apart from Dorian Faulk's supervision. The cheap next step, £9k of confidential interviews, is clear, though putting off both remedies risks losing more people in the meantime.
